name: scatter_sora
description: Sora (Saora) — a South Munda language of the Eastern Ghats and Rushikulya basin (Odisha, Andhra Pradesh), written in its own Sorang Sompeng script as well as Odia, Telugu, and Roman; structurally distinct from the North Munda cluster (Santali, Mundari, Ho, Korku). On the standardized 12-column place axis. The South Munda branch does NOT carry a robust retroflex stop contrast — Sora's stop inventory runs only across 4 places (bilabial, dental, palatal, velar), and the retroflex column is empty in the stop rows. Voiceless / voiced stop pairs at 4 places. Four matched nasals (m, n, ɲ, ŋ). Sibilant /s/, glottal /h/, lateral /l/, trill /r/, glides /w, j/. Inventory follows Anderson (2008) and Donegan & Stampe; some descriptions add a marginal glottal stop /ʔ/ and aspirated stops in Indic loans (not shown here, to keep the cells phonemic). 18 cells filled — sparser than North Munda by exactly the retroflex stop pair, which is the structural signature distinguishing the two Munda branches.
